Formula labels (4) and (5) share their formula baselines and are not counted twice; the overwritten Omega shares line 2.

changes.evidence: The short upper curl joins a single long inflected descending stroke. Root compared this with all six occurrences on scan105, whose sentence continues here. Zeta remains visually preferred; reduced xi remains possible, so the same unresolved alternatives are used across both pages.

changes.place: physical line 1 / choice of the point
changes.evidence: After the joined humps of un comes a small looped crossing x, an upright membership sign with a horizontal middle stroke, and a large crossed X. There is no intervening pt and no two-letter de. The crop includes d’un and the entire mathematical phrase.
changes.error_category: Text that is not on the page

changes.evidence: The underlying upright and two rightward oblique limbs of K are individually visible beneath a broad rounded arch ending in horizontal feet. A separate high bar belongs to the underlying barred K in the proposed layering. The surviving arch is read as capital Omega; the temporal attribution of the high bar is less secure than the letters themselves. No material of the overwritten K is suppressed.

changes.H: (par ex. une clôture alg. de $k(x)$) et on

changes.evidence: The first word has a descending p and two low terminal strokes; the next has the n/e body, a detached accent, c, and a stop, supporting pas néc. The short word before clôture is visibly overwritten/cancelled by jagged strokes. Its probable une is retained as doubtful because the cancellation prevents each letter being isolated. The following alg. and de k(x) remain live.

changes.place: physical line 4 / note and alternate notation
changes.C: note alors aussi $\mathcal E_X^\Omega$ au lieu de
changes.final: note alors aussi $\mathcal E_X^\Omega$ au lieu de
changes.evidence: Between note and aussi is a separately spaced word with a tall initial a/l-like rise and low terminal rs strokes: alors. After the complete E_X^Omega the ink is a small initial mark and low joined u, followed by the tall l, dotted i and connected eu of lieu. This supports au lieu de, not a dash standing by itself. The subscript is a large crossed X and the superscript an open-footed Omega.

changes.place: physical line 5 / Greek-indexed expression and qualification
changes.evidence: The line begins with a complete E, crossed X below, and a thin descending Greek sign above. An opening parenthesis and capital Omega follow. There is a separate short hyphen between sous and entendu, followed by the small word en and the tall initial/terminal strokes of tant; the final qu has a long q descender and an apostrophe. The Greek sign remains xi/zeta uncertain; the words are legible. H’s notation/au/illegible sequence does not follow these letter groups. Root retains the same zeta-first alternative order as scan105 after visually comparing the continuing notation.

changes.place: physical lines 6–8 / explanation, inserted phrase, and On aura
changes.C: extension de $k(x)$, donc avec sa structure de $k(x)$ algèbre). On aura \inserted{un isom can.}
changes.final: extension de $k(x)$, donc avec sa structure de $k(x)$ algèbre). On aura \inserted{un isom \unsure{can|can.}}
changes.evidence: The upper main baseline has extension de, k(x), a comma, donc, avec, a small sa, and structure with tall t strokes. The next main baseline has de k(x) algèbre), with the g descender and short terminal e; there is no long -brique ending. On is followed by the low separated strokes of aura. Above aura the phrase reads un isom can; a curved leader runs beneath it and turns down after aura, attaching the insertion there. No detached stop after can can be isolated; the final downward endpoint may belong to the final letter, so can|can. remains marked in place.

changes.place: physical line 9 / entire formula (4), first subscript
changes.evidence: The first lower index has a closed left loop, an upward-right diagonal, and a down-right exit, unlike the two long open diagonals of the adjacent capital X. It is alpha-like; a cursive lowercase x remains possible because some x shapes inside k(x) on this leaf also close on the left. The manuscript does not warrant capital X here. Both complete E expressions, the barred k(x), the isomorphism sign, the numeral 4, and the concluding comma were inspected. The alpha/x distinction remains undecided.

The abbreviation after clôture has a small angular initial a, a tall looped l and a rounded descending g, then a distinct stop. There is no accented e or long p ascender/descender combination for sép. The preceding circumflex over clôture is present.

After notation the short initial s is followed by low connected ur strokes and two tall t strokes separated by the rounded ou group. The terminal t runs near the right paper edge. These strokes support surtout; standard would require a different initial st/a group and a terminal d loop.

changes.place: physical lines 15–16 / Y connexe insertion and live on notera
changes.evidence: The long curve begins between the preceding comma and on, rises under Y connexe, and ends to the right of its comma. It is an insertion leader. It does not cross on. The thick horizontal strokes in notera follow the joined letter bodies; its tall t intersects the leader but there is no separate cancellation traversing the two words. Y connexe therefore attaches before the live on notera.

changes.place: physical line 17 / entire formula (5), morphism shaft
changes.evidence: The shaft after E_X ends at the right in a short dark downward barb, not a uniform terminal stroke. The same small barb occurs on the final-line category arrow. The f:X→Y arrow at the right has a more prominent head. Both ends, all labels, and numeral 5 were inspected. A rightward arrow is proposed for the faint-headed first shaft.

changes.place: physical line 19 / abbreviated category expression and arrow
changes.evidence: The source has the compact letter group Sch followed by a space and conn; there are no letters émas or exes. The target has g with a descending loop, r, p with a long descender and compressed es, followed by a separate ext group whose last t rises and returns to the baseline. No final detached stop is present. The connecting shaft has a short downward terminal barb at the right. Both parenthesis marks belong to Sch conn; no closing parenthesis for the larger preceding parenthetical sentence is visible.
Thin lower-left numerals show 1, a closed oval0, and a5 with short upper bar and rounded lower curve. This is separate foliation, not an authorial page number at the head of the sheet.

decisions.evidence: The initial Greek sign has a small upper curl and a very long descending stem; the middle articulation is too slight to discriminate xi from zeta confidently using this leaf alone. Root compared the same reduced form on preceding scan105, whose sentence continues here; zeta is consistently preferred without excluding xi.

The superscript repeats the thin descending form with two short upper kinks; the entire E_X superscript expression was inspected. It does not settle the xi/zeta distinction. Root compared the same reduced form on preceding scan105, whose sentence continues here; zeta is consistently preferred without excluding xi.

The subscript has a closed left loop and is smaller and differently formed from the clear capital X to its right. Alpha remains the first candidate; lowercase x replaces capital X as the alternative, since looped x forms also occur in k(x). No complete resolution is claimed.
Only Sch and conn are inked, with an actual space between them. There is no émas continuation or other ink to support Schémas. The surrounding parentheses, arrow, and target were read together.
A descending g, r, a long-descending p, then compact es are followed by a separate ext ending in tall t. The entire category expression was inspected; no final punctuation is visible.

notes: This continuing manuscript leaf describes the notation E_X^Omega associated with a point and a separably closed extension, gives formula (4), mentions the affine and field notation, and starts functorial notation E(f) with formula (5). The last parenthetical sentence remains open at the foot of the leaf.

Only this page packet was read. No other page, OCR, external research, PDF text layer, or TeX compilation was used. Full image and each native half were inspected once, followed by the fourteen recorded contextual crops.

The count is 20 written baselines under the root all-ink convention: 17 main baselines, two supralinear insertion baselines, and the standalone lower-left 105. Formula numerals share their display lines. The small numeral 105 is preserved; its hand cannot be independently attributed from this leaf alone.
The leader under un isom can attaches after aura; the leader under Y connexe attaches before on notera. Neither leader is transcribed as punctuation or as a cancellation of the underlying live words.

The line 2 symbol is visibly an overwrite of barred K by Omega. The proposed temporal allocation of the high bar to the underlying K is medium-confidence; H instead reads barred Omega and omits the underlying K.

In formula (4), alpha-like ink is retained with lowercase x as alternative. Other nearby expressions use capital X; this alone does not justify changing the written subscript. Capital X is written in a visibly different open crossing form.
The deletion doubt une is present in C.tex but absent from marks.tsv; it is retained in the transcription and remaining-doubts list, without inventing a MARKS identifier.

Several tight contextual crops include tips of descenders or subscripts from a neighbouring baseline at an edge. Such clipped continuations are not duplicated as new source words in the transcription. Audit b06 extends slightly lower than its contextual crop to include the full subscript; audit b11 isolates the actual insertion and the words on notera from the wider line crop.

No independent mathematical proof verification was performed. Reading a familiar expression was not used as a reason to restore missing letters, expand abbreviations, or regularize the first subscript of (4).

Root adjudication aligns the unresolved geometric-point letter with scan105 as zeta|xi, after inspecting both pages. The bottom105 is retained with the margin macro, because it is foliation rather than an authorial heading number. The first map shaft in(5) is read as a lightly headed arrow, at medium confidence; it remains an independent-audit target.
